title: Salmon on a Sheet Pan With Brussels Sprouts
description: From Food & Wine: “I get excited making this dinner because it’s easy, full of flavor, and a good balance of sweet, sour, and spicy—depending on how much cayenne pepper you add. Start with a small pinch to start, then add more if you prefer a spicy kick. That’s the great part about cooking for yourself—you can crank up the heat as much as you want! But the true beauty of the recipe is that it all cooks on one sheet pan and just takes about 20 minutes. So when dinner’s done, there’s just one pan to wash. Then you can get back to unwinding with your favorite tunes and that well-deserved glass of wine.”
ingredients: 1 tablespoon minced peeled fresh ginger (from 1 [2-inch] piece)
12 medium brussels sprouts, trimmed and cut into 1/4-inch-thick slices (about 1 1/4 cups)
1 or 2 small red bell pepper (about 6 ounces), cut into 1/4-inch-thick strips (about 1 cup)
1 cup thinly sliced red onion (from 1 small onion)
2/3 pound skin-on salmon fillet (about 1 inch thick)
directions: Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
Whisk together hoisin sauce, lime juice, 2 tablespoons oil, ginger, garlic, and cayenne in a small bowl; set aside.
Toss together brussels sprouts, bell pepper, onion, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and remaining 2 tablespoons oil.
Place salmon on prepared sheet pan. Arrange vegetable mixture around salmon.
Drizzle some of the hoisin mixture on salmon and vegetable mixture; reserve remaining hoisin mixture.
Bake until salmon is cooked to desired degree of doneness and vegetables are tender, 16 to 20 minutes.
Drizzle some reserved hoisin mixture over salmon and vegetables, and sprinkle salmon with salt to taste.
